worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
{(1+x)}^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-\frac{2k}{3}$ and $n=7$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-\frac{2k}{3})}^{7} & =1+7\cdot (-\frac{2k}{3})+\frac{7(7-1)}{2!}\cdot {(-\frac{2k}{3})}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{14k}{3}+\frac{7\cdot 6}{2}\cdot \frac{4{k}^{2}}{9}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{14k}{3}+21\cdot \frac{4{k}^{2}}{9}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{14k}{3}+\frac{28{k}^{2}}{3}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
